reports.title: NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for Third Quarter Fiscal 2027

guidance.heading: Outlook
section: NVIDIA’s outlook for the fourth quarter of fiscal 2027, which includes an additional week, is as follows:
•Revenue is expected to be $130.0 billion, plus or minus 3%. NVIDIA is not assuming any Data Center compute revenue from China in its outlook.
•GAAP and non-GAAP gross margins are expected to be between 71.0% and 72.0%.
•GAAP and non-GAAP operating expenses are expected to be approximately $11.0 billion and $10.7 billion, respectively.
•For the full year fiscal 2027, NVIDIA expects GAAP and non-GAAP tax rates to be between 16.0% and 18.0%, excluding any discrete items and material changes to NVIDIA’s tax environment.

desk.headline: Revenue up 103% to $115.8bn, EPS beat; Q4 outlook $130bn ±3%

other.label: Returned to shareholders
other.change: buybacks and dividends in the quarter

results: Revenue roughly doubled to a record $115.8bn, up 20% from Q2, led by Data Center sales of $107.6bn.
The new Vera Rubin platform began shipping in what the company calls its fastest product ramp; Blackwell Ultra kept growing.
Non-GAAP gross margin was 74.9%, up 1.4 points on the year but slightly lower than Q2 as Rubin production ramped.
Free cash flow was $43.8bn; $28.1bn went back to shareholders and the buyback authorisation was raised by $150bn ($227.3bn left).
Supply commitments rose to $390bn from $279bn, mainly multi-year memory purchases, and maximum guarantee exposure is $118bn, including up to $105bn for a data-centre campus leased to OpenAI.

guidance.summary: For Q4 (a 14-week quarter) NVIDIA expects revenue of about $130bn, plus or minus 3%, with gross margin of 71-72%. The outlook assumes no Data Center compute sales to China.

points: Growth came from both hyperscalers ($60.1bn, +71% y/y) and AI clouds, industrial and enterprise customers ($47.5bn, +195% y/y).
Hopper data-centre shipments to China were $2.4bn in the quarter, but none is assumed in the Q4 outlook.
Receivables rose to 64 days of sales as Rubin shipments came late in the quarter and some large customers got longer payment terms.
Inventory rose to $39.7bn from $31.6bn to support the Rubin ramp.
Higher memory and system prices continue to weigh on consumer PC demand.

watch: Q4 gross margin as Rubin output scales (guided down to 71-72%).
Rising receivables, supply commitments and customer guarantees.
Leadership transition under interim CEO Colette Kress and the independent board committee investigation.
